entries.title: POST response omits a field the request itself declared
entries.rationale: GOLDEN_REPAIR_CORPUS_DEFINITION.md §2 row 1: a POST handler's own real jsonify response contract must include every field the request body itself supplied; removing one is a real, structural contract violation any generated_backend_tests run should be able to surface.

entries.title: PUT/DELETE mutates a non-existent record with no existence guard
entries.rationale: GOLDEN_REPAIR_CORPUS_DEFINITION.md §2 row 2: removing the existence guard lets a mutation 'succeed' against a record that was never in the required prior state -- a real invalid state transition.

entries.title: Access-control (CORS) boundary silently disabled
entries.rationale: The mandatory unrepairable entry (corpus definition §4). No pytest test in this pipeline's own generated tests/ suite (Flask test_client only) ever asserts on CORS/access-control headers, so a bounded repair strategy gets no real test-based convergence signal for this specific class the way it does for the other seven -- the same repeated-strategy/budget-exhaustion path (RepeatedFailedStrategyError / RepairBudgetExceededError, both already real in contracts.py) is expected to fire and reach terminal ESCALATED for this entry specifically, proving bounded non-convergence rather than an unbounded retry loop.

entries.title: INSERT reaches the connection but is never committed
entries.rationale: GOLDEN_REPAIR_CORPUS_DEFINITION.md §2 row 4: a write that never durably commits fails the real sqlite_restart_persistence check any real acceptance journey already performs.

entries.title: Declared route contract no longer matches the real backend route
entries.rationale: GOLDEN_REPAIR_CORPUS_DEFINITION.md §2 row 5: backend/routes.json is the real, machine-readable route contract every frontend/E2E consumer trusts; drifting it from the backend's own real @app.route declarations is a genuine API/frontend contract break.

entries.title: Flask pin widened past its verified compatible Werkzeug range
entries.rationale: golden-work-077 (real, frozen session evidence, dependency_resolution.py module docstring): flask==2.x with no Werkzeug<3 cap installs cleanly but genuinely fails Flask's own test_client() against Werkzeug 3.x -- a real, previously-observed dependency/lock mismatch, reused here as the injected corpus defect.

entries.title: Live CREATE TABLE schema drops a field data_model.json still declares
entries.rationale: GOLDEN_REPAIR_CORPUS_DEFINITION.md §2 row 7: the live schema migration (backend/db.py) and the declared data model (backend/data_model.json) are two real, independently-generated artifacts that must agree; dropping a column from one is a genuine migration/model mismatch.

entries.title: Parameterised route loses its integer type boundary
entries.rationale: GOLDEN_REPAIR_CORPUS_DEFINITION.md §2 row 8: Flask's own <int:...> converter is the real boundary/type check protecting every id-addressed route; widening it to an untyped segment lets a non-integer id reach a query built to expect one.
